children: U.S. Treasury yields surged Wednesday as investors sold bonds across the curve. The benchmark U.S. 10 Year Treasury yield
climbed 16 basis points to 5.12%, breaking above well above 5% and reaching its highest recorded level since July 2007.
The more rate-sensitive U.S. 2 Year Treasury yield
jumped 18 basis points to 4.93%, while the U.S. 30 Year Treasury yield
added 10 basis points and traded at 5.40%

The coordinated advance reflected market pricing of a stronger growth backdrop and reduced odds of near-term Federal Reserve easing. Bond prices and yields move inversely; the latest selling pressure lifted longer-dated yields to multi-year highs as participants reassessed the path for policy and inflation.

Supporting the move, S&P Global’s services PMI jumped to 58.7 in September from 56.5 in August, the highest reading in nearly five years. The companion manufacturing index rose to 56.7, a level last seen more than four years ago. Both prints pointed to broadening private-sector momentum and reinforced the view that the economy remains resilient.
